VACATION IN CHICAGO LEADS TO JAIL
Hays Yancey, age 20, while only in the city two days visiting from New Orleans, La., has already fallen into the hands of the law. Yancey, it is claimed, by Sergeant Scott of the bureau, went to call on his lady friend with a "Black Jack" in his pocket. It appears that he sought to fondle her with this "Black Jack" and drew from her a protest saying it was not Chicago style, and he is now spending his vacation at the bridewell. While attempting to act as mediator in a family quarrel between mother and father Lorenzo Davis, age 22, 3745 Vernon Ave., was struck with a glass pitcher thrown by his father. While suffering from an epileptic fit, Mrs. Lizzie Sanford, age 55, 111 South Bishop St. was removed to the county hospital, July 30. Miss Anna Hughes was the center of attraction at 5031 Federal St. until William Thornton, age 50, and said to have been an ardent wooer, pressed his attention with too much vigor. Mr. Thornton, who resides at 1608 Jefferson St., Gary, Ind., had not taken into consideration the fact that a certain Mr. Will Douglas was also paying court to the fair Anna. He is cognizant of it now as Douglas made the impression with a knife, results of which Thornton is now at the Provident Hospital, cut in the left breast, eight inches long. All went well for Richard Gallagher, age 21, 511 East 37th St., while visiting friends at 4233 Wabash Ave. until he ruffled the feathers of Henry Shannon, who resented it with a water pitcher, causing a severe wound on the left side of Gallagher's head, also disfiguring the upper lip. Mr. Gallagher is concluding his visit at the Provident Hospital. Mrs. Cora Wells, age 39, 4834 State St., in a quarrel with her husband was severely kicked and beaten, sustaining internal injuries as a result. She was treated by Dr. Dillom of Provident Hospital, and is said to have caused the arrest of her husband. Claude Cheeks, age 36, 5204 South Dearborn St., was severely beaten while under arrest by several officers of the 48th St. Station sustaining severe injuries of the head, and was removed to Provident Hospital. Clarence McDuff, 2832 Federal St., was shot and badly wounded by his wife, at 38th and State St. Monday afternoon. While the bullets were passing thick and fast, William Hulbert, a bystander, was struck in the head by a stray bullet. Along with McDuff he was taken to the county hospital. The cause for the attempted murder could not be ascertained. Sgt. Frank Starks, of the detective bureau, left Saturday night for New York City to bring back Rev. R. D. Jonas, who is alleged to have passed some bogus checks on William Jones, a gracer at 3636 South State Street. It will be recalled that Dr. Jonas fled the city during /the investigation of the "Abyssinian" affair. Henry Johnson, age 25, 3160 Wabash Ave., stopped at 32nd and State Sts. Friday night to purchase a sandwich from Harold Taylor, the proprietor of a sandwich wagon. During the transaction Johnson is alleged to have questioned the manner in which he was being served and approached Taylor in a threatening manner with a knife. It was then that Taylor drew from beneath his apron a revolver and fired several times, one bullet taking effect in Johnson's hip, and a stray bullet piercing the body of James Peyton, 3810 Prairie Ave. Both were taken to the county hospital. James Woddie, 1910 Fulton St., 24 years old, was shot Sunday night as a result of a quarrel over 50 cents in a pool room at Lake and Robey Sts. He was struck twice, both bullets passing through his right lung. His assailant escaped. Mrs. Celia Lewis, age 46, 2827 State St., while temporarily latewinter, wrecked all the windows in nearby stores at 28th and State St., July 27. After having completed the job, she was removed to the psychopathic hospital for observation. Mrs. Mabel Stone, age 26, 3648 Grand Blvd., was struck by a horse and buggy, July 28, at 35th and State Sts. She was severely injured.
